Please review the following manuscript.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b07/review-experiment-nlzm6avz/call-484c7c4cc3bd4e1683578a39b084bafa/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES:',len(reader.pages))
for i,p in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
    t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+p.read_text() for i,p in enumerate(sorted(Path('tmp/pdfs').glob('page-*.txt')),1)))
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('tmp/pdfs')
for f in p.iterdir():
    if f.is_file() and f.suffix in {'.txt', '.png'}:
        f.unlink()
p.rmdir()
Path('tmp').rmdir()
PY"

strengths: The joint study of clean generalization, robust training fit, and robust test error addresses an important problem, with explicit definitions of the target phenomenon.
Separating shared signal learning from sample-specific noise memorization offers an interpretable candidate mechanism. The feature coordinates U and V make the proposed training phases concrete.
The experiments include synthetic feature trajectories and complementary capacity and local-flatness measurements on MNIST and CIFAR10, providing useful qualitative observations.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.4 is false under Assumptions 4.1–4.3 alone. Consider a balanced distribution on X=±e1 with labels ±1, δ=1/4, and f_clean(X)=X_1−0.9. This satisfies boundedness, separation, zero clean error, and robust error 1/2. As N grows, both atoms have nonvanishing empirical frequency, so o(1) robust training error forces zero robust population error; a CGRO classifier cannot exist. Additional assumptions controlling training-neighborhood coverage are needed. Appendix F also incorrectly asserts uniform approximation of a generally discontinuous f_S by continuous ReLU networks.

Theorem 5.9 conflates robustness to restricted signal-aligned attacks with robustness to the full norm ball in Definitions 3.2–3.4. Appendix E.12 transfers small restricted training loss to full robust training accuracy without justification. Indeed, the claimed feature behavior contradicts full ℓ2 robustness: the total noisy-patch norm r is o(α), so reversing those patches and reducing the signal to β=α−sqrt(δ²−4r²)=o(α) is a feasible radius-δ attack. For the stated odd-q model, its signed margin is proportional to β^q U−V_i<0 under the theorem's claimed U and V_i.

The clean-generalization proof in Appendix E.12 contains additional substantive gaps. General cubic Gaussian projections are not sub-Gaussian, and projections across filters share the same test patches, so the displayed concentration bound is unjustified. Furthermore, V_i=Θ(1) does not imply that every residual weight vector has norm Θ(1), as asserted. These steps are essential to the claimed o(1) clean test error and require a corrected probabilistic argument with explicit scaling conditions.

The flatness-only generalization bound in Theorem B.1 is also invalid as stated. A nonzero constant classifier has zero input gradients, while its logistic loss still depends on the sampled labels. Its empirical risk can therefore fall below its population risk with probability approaching one half. The proposed bound has zero slack in this example and cannot hold with high probability; it omits ordinary sampling fluctuations.

The synthetic experiment does not validate the theorem's assumptions: Section 6.2 sets δ=α=10, contradicting the strict δ<α requirement in Assumption 5.7 and permitting complete removal of the meaningful signal. With label-independent noise, poor performance on these attacked inputs follows from information removal. The image experiments also do not distinguish representation limitations from optimization failure, particularly for the chance-level MNIST models. Missing PGD step counts, step sizes, restart settings, and variability across runs limit reproducibility and assessment of the robustness measurements.

The claimed extension of the representation lower bound over Li et al. (2022) is unclear. Theorem 4.7 remains existential, and Appendix F still constructs a linearly separable instance. Enlarging the admissible class to distributions with a polynomial-size clean classifier does not itself strengthen that earlier lower bound. The relevance of this worst-case result to the image-capacity experiments also needs clearer justification.
